title: Articles: the mixed cases
note: Built 2026-08-22 (James, interactive) from the articles error-correction sheet used in Václav's lesson (15 sentences, 28 errors) — one item per error, the other error in the sentence shown corrected. Mixed case families on purpose: first-mention a/an vs known `the` (8) · `the` forced by of-phrase / superlative / date / compass (7) · a few, jobs (2) · names with and without `the` (5) · institutions, meals, last weekend (4) · general plural/uncountable (2). Zero-article items gap article+noun so the bare form is the answer (b1_articles_advanced convention). Dropped: `in the hotel` → `a hotel` (both readable). Also shipped as a standalone practice HTML for Padlet (Václav, Martina, Tomas).

items.en: I am reading an interesting book at the moment.
items.cz: Právě čtu zajímavou knihu.
items.gap: I am reading ____ interesting book at the moment.
accepts: I am reading an interesting book at the moment.
items.explanation: First mention = a/an. The listener does not know which one yet.
items.explanation_cz: První zmínka = a/an. Posluchač ještě neví, o který jde.

items.en: I went to the cinema last night with a friend from work.
items.cz: Včera večer jsem šel do kina s kamarádem z práce.
items.gap: I went to the cinema last night with ____ friend from work.
accepts: I went to the cinema last night with a friend from work.
items.explanation: First mention = a/an. The listener does not know which one yet.
items.explanation_cz: První zmínka = a/an. Posluchač ještě neví, o který jde.

items.en: I've only been inside a church once, when I went to Russia.
items.cz: Uvnitř kostela jsem byl jen jednou, když jsem jel do Ruska.
items.gap: I've only been inside ____ church once, when I went to Russia.
accepts: I've only been inside a church once, when I went to Russia.
items.explanation: `a church` = the building, one of many. `go to church` (no article) is the activity.
items.explanation_cz: `a church` = budova, jedna z mnoha. `go to church` (bez členu) je činnost.

items.en: I've started going to a yoga class on Thursdays. The teacher is very good.
items.cz: Začal jsem chodit ve čtvrtek na jógu. Učitelka je velmi dobrá.
items.gap: I've started going to a yoga class on Thursdays. ____ teacher is very good.
accepts: I've started going to a yoga class on Thursdays. The teacher is very good.
items.explanation: `the` = we both know which one: it was mentioned before, or the situation makes it obvious.
items.explanation_cz: `the` = oba víme, který: už byl zmíněn, nebo je ze situace jasný.

items.en: I've got two pets, a cat and a dog. I don't like the cat.
items.cz: Mám dva mazlíčky, kočku a psa. Kočku nemám rád.
items.gap: I've got two pets, a cat and a dog. I don't like ____ cat.
accepts: I've got two pets, a cat and a dog. I don't like the cat.
items.explanation: `the` = we both know which one: it was mentioned before, or the situation makes it obvious.
items.explanation_cz: `the` = oba víme, který: už byl zmíněn, nebo je ze situace jasný.

items.en: The police should be given the money they need to deal with the problem.
items.cz: Policie by měla dostat peníze, které potřebuje na řešení toho problému.
items.gap: The police should be given the money they need to deal with ____ problem.
accepts: The police should be given the money they need to deal with the problem.
items.explanation: `the` = we both know which one: it was mentioned before, or the situation makes it obvious.
items.explanation_cz: `the` = oba víme, který: už byl zmíněn, nebo je ze situace jasný.

items.en: You may now open the examination paper.
items.cz: Nyní můžete otevřít zkouškový arch.
items.gap: You may now open ____ examination paper.
accepts: You may now open the examination paper.
items.explanation: `the` = we both know which one: it was mentioned before, or the situation makes it obvious.
items.explanation_cz: `the` = oba víme, který: už byl zmíněn, nebo je ze situace jasný.

items.en: Have you been to the new cycle shop on Regent Street?
items.cz: Byl jsi už v tom novém cykloobchodě na Regent Street?
items.gap: Have you been to ____ new cycle shop on Regent Street?
accepts: Have you been to the new cycle shop on Regent Street?
items.explanation: `the` = we both know which one: it was mentioned before, or the situation makes it obvious.
items.explanation_cz: `the` = oba víme, který: už byl zmíněn, nebo je ze situace jasný.

items.en: It's about the life of Nelson Mandela when he was in prison.
items.cz: Je to o životě Nelsona Mandely, když byl ve vězení.
items.gap: It's about ____ life of Nelson Mandela when he was in prison.
accepts: It's about the life of Nelson Mandela when he was in prison.
items.explanation: `the` + noun + of …: the of-phrase says which one, so it is definite.
items.explanation_cz: `the` + podstatné jméno + of …: vazba s of říká, který — proto určitý člen.

items.en: There's a restaurant in the centre of Washington.
items.cz: V centru Washingtonu je jedna restaurace.
items.gap: There's a restaurant in ____ centre of Washington.
accepts: There's a restaurant in the centre of Washington.
items.explanation: `the` + noun + of …: the of-phrase says which one, so it is definite.
items.explanation_cz: `the` + podstatné jméno + of …: vazba s of říká, který — proto určitý člen.

items.en: Write your name and the date at the top of the page.
items.cz: Napište své jméno a datum do horní části stránky.
items.gap: Write your name and the date at ____ top of the page.
accepts: Write your name and the date at the top of the page.
items.explanation: `the` + noun + of …: the of-phrase says which one, so it is definite.
items.explanation_cz: `the` + podstatné jméno + of …: vazba s of říká, který — proto určitý člen.

items.en: While I was staying in a hotel in the south of India, I met a man who worked for the CIA.
items.cz: Když jsem bydlel v hotelu na jihu Indie, potkal jsem muže, který pracoval pro CIA.
items.gap: While I was staying in a hotel in ____ south of India, I met a man who worked for the CIA.
accepts: While I was staying in a hotel in the south of India, I met a man who worked for the CIA.
While I was living in a hotel in the south of India, I met a man who worked for the CIA.
items.explanation: the north / the south / the east / the west of a place — always `the`.
items.explanation_cz: the north / the south / the east / the west + of — vždy `the`.

items.en: It makes the most delicious lasagne in the world.
items.cz: Dělají nejlepší lasagne na světě.
items.gap: It makes ____ most delicious lasagne in the world.
accepts: It makes the most delicious lasagne in the world.
items.explanation: Superlatives take `the`: the best, the worst, the most delicious.
items.explanation_cz: Superlativ má `the`: the best, the worst, the most delicious.

items.en: The teacher is very good, but I'm the worst in the class.
items.cz: Učitelka je velmi dobrá, ale já jsem ve třídě nejhorší.
items.gap: The teacher is very good, but I'm ____ worst in the class.
accepts: The teacher is very good, but I'm the worst in the class.
items.explanation: Superlatives take `the`: the best, the worst, the most delicious.
items.explanation_cz: Superlativ má `the`: the best, the worst, the most delicious.

items.en: Mark and Laura got married on the twenty-third of December.
items.cz: Mark a Laura se vzali dvacátého třetího prosince.
items.gap: Mark and Laura got married on ____ twenty-third of December.
accepts: Mark and Laura got married on the twenty-third of December.
items.explanation: Dates said in full: on the twenty-third of December. Ordinals take `the`.
items.explanation_cz: Datum vyslovené celé: on the twenty-third of December. Řadové číslovky mají `the`.

items.en: A few days later, Laura realised she'd made the worst decision of her life.
items.cz: O několik dní později si Laura uvědomila, že udělala nejhorší rozhodnutí svého života.
items.gap: ____ few days later, Laura realised she'd made the worst decision of her life.
accepts: A few days later, Laura realised she'd made the worst decision of her life.
items.explanation: `a few` = some (neutral). `few` without `a` = hardly any (negative).
items.explanation_cz: `a few` = několik (neutrální). `few` bez `a` = sotva nějaké (záporné).

items.en: After leaving school, Janet worked as a cleaner in a hospital.
items.cz: Po škole Janet pracovala jako uklízečka v nemocnici.
items.gap: After leaving school, Janet worked as ____ cleaner in a hospital.
accepts: After leaving school, Janet worked as a cleaner in a hospital.
items.explanation: Jobs take a/an: work as a cleaner, she is a nurse. Czech has nothing here.
items.explanation_cz: Povolání má a/an: work as a cleaner, she is a nurse. Čeština tu nemá nic.

items.en: Last weekend, Janet Morgan went skiing in the Alps and then stayed in a hotel by Lake Geneva.
items.cz: Minulý víkend jela Janet Morgan lyžovat do Alp a pak bydlela v hotelu u Ženevského jezera.
items.gap: Last weekend, Janet Morgan went skiing in ____ and then stayed in a hotel by Lake Geneva.
accepts: Last weekend, Janet Morgan went skiing in the Alps and then stayed in a hotel by Lake Geneva.
Last weekend, Janet Morgan went skiing in the Alps and then lived in a hotel by Lake Geneva.
items.explanation: `the` with mountain ranges, wars, theatres, newspapers and organisations: the Alps, the Vietnam War, the National Theatre.
items.explanation_cz: `the` u pohoří, válek, divadel, novin a organizací: the Alps, the Vietnam War, the National Theatre.

items.en: We saw a film about the Vietnam War.
items.cz: Viděli jsme film o vietnamské válce.
items.gap: We saw a film about ____.
accepts: We saw a film about the Vietnam War.
items.explanation: `the` with mountain ranges, wars, theatres, newspapers and organisations: the Alps, the Vietnam War, the National Theatre.
items.explanation_cz: `the` u pohoří, válek, divadel, novin a organizací: the Alps, the Vietnam War, the National Theatre.

items.en: As I was walking along Oxford Street on my way to the National Theatre, I found a ten-pound note on the pavement.
items.cz: Když jsem šel po Oxford Street do Národního divadla, našel jsem na chodníku desetilibrovou bankovku.
items.gap: As I was walking along Oxford Street on my way to ____, I found a ten-pound note on the pavement.
accepts: As I was walking along Oxford Street on my way to the National Theatre, I found a ten-pound note on the pavement.
items.explanation: `the` with mountain ranges, wars, theatres, newspapers and organisations: the Alps, the Vietnam War, the National Theatre.
items.explanation_cz: `the` u pohoří, válek, divadel, novin a organizací: the Alps, the Vietnam War, the National Theatre.

items.en: I found a ten-pound note on the pavement.
items.cz: Našel jsem na chodníku desetilibrovou bankovku.
items.gap: I found a ten-pound note on ____ pavement.
accepts: I found a ten-pound note on the pavement.
items.explanation: `the pavement` — the one you are walking on. Obvious from the situation.
items.explanation_cz: `the pavement` — ten, po kterém jdete. Jasné ze situace.

items.en: Have you been to the new cycle shop on Regent Street?
items.cz: Byl jsi už v tom novém cykloobchodě na Regent Street?
items.gap: Have you been to the new cycle shop on ____?
accepts: Have you been to the new cycle shop on Regent Street?
items.explanation: Streets, lakes, cities and most countries take no article: Regent Street, Lake Geneva, Washington, India.
items.explanation_cz: Ulice, jezera, města a většina zemí jsou bez členu: Regent Street, Lake Geneva, Washington, India.

items.en: I don't go to church.
items.cz: Nechodím do kostela.
items.gap: I don't go to ____.
accepts: I don't go to church.
items.explanation: go to church / school / college / hospital (as a user of it) — no article. `the church` = the building.
items.explanation_cz: go to church / school / college / hospital (jako jejich uživatel) — bez členu. `the church` = budova.

items.en: She then went to college to study nursing.
items.cz: Potom šla na vysokou školu studovat ošetřovatelství.
items.gap: She then went to ____ to study nursing.
accepts: She then went to college to study nursing.
items.explanation: go to church / school / college / hospital (as a user of it) — no article. `the church` = the building.
items.explanation_cz: go to church / school / college / hospital (jako jejich uživatel) — bez členu. `the church` = budova.

items.en: "What do you want for dinner?" "Nothing, thanks. I met an old friend from school and we had lunch together."
items.cz: „Co chceš k večeři?“ „Nic, díky. Potkal jsem starého kamaráda ze školy a byli jsme spolu na obědě.“
items.gap: "What do you want for ____?" "Nothing, thanks. I met an old friend from school and we had lunch together."
accepts: "What do you want for dinner?" "Nothing, thanks. I met an old friend from school and we had lunch together."
items.explanation: Meals take no article: for dinner, have lunch, after breakfast.
items.explanation_cz: Jídla jsou bez členu: for dinner, have lunch, after breakfast.

items.en: Last weekend, Janet Morgan went skiing in the Alps.
items.cz: Minulý víkend jela Janet Morgan lyžovat do Alp.
items.gap: ____, Janet Morgan went skiing in the Alps.
accepts: Last weekend, Janet Morgan went skiing in the Alps.
items.explanation: last / next / this + time word takes no article: last weekend, next week, this morning.
items.explanation_cz: last / next / this + časový výraz je bez členu: last weekend, next week, this morning.

items.en: I don't like the cat, because he brings mice into the house.
items.cz: Kočku nemám rád, protože nosí do domu myši.
items.gap: I don't like the cat, because he brings ____ into the house.
accepts: I don't like the cat, because he brings mice into the house.
items.explanation: Talking in general: plural or uncountable noun with no article. `the` would mean particular ones.
items.explanation_cz: Obecně: množné číslo nebo nepočitatelné jméno bez členu. `the` by znamenalo konkrétní.

items.en: Many of the cities in the USA suffer from crime.
items.cz: Mnoho měst v USA trpí kriminalitou.
items.gap: Many of the cities in the USA suffer from ____.
accepts: Many of the cities in the USA suffer from crime.
items.explanation: Talking in general: plural or uncountable noun with no article. `the` would mean particular ones.
items.explanation_cz: Obecně: množné číslo nebo nepočitatelné jméno bez členu. `the` by znamenalo konkrétní.

cards.title: First mention a/an, then the
cards.body: When you bring something into the conversation, it gets a/an. Once the listener knows which one, it gets `the`. Czech has no articles, so the whole job is asking: does the listener already know which one?
cards.body_cz: Když něco do hovoru uvedete, dostane a/an. Jakmile posluchač ví, o které jde, dostane `the`. Čeština členy nemá, takže celá práce je ptát se: ví už posluchač, o které jde?

rows: I went out with a friend from work.
I've got a cat and a dog.
I go to a yoga class.

cards.title: `the` forced by the structure
cards.body: Some structures make the noun definite on their own, so `the` is automatic — even on first mention.
cards.body_cz: Některé vazby dělají jméno určitým samy o sobě, takže `the` je automatické — i při první zmínce.
points: noun + of: the life of Mandela · the centre of Washington · the top of the page
superlative: the best · the worst · the most delicious lasagne
dates said in full: on the twenty-third of December
compass + of: the south of India · the north of England
obvious from the situation: on the pavement · open the examination paper

cards.title: Names: which ones take `the`?
cards.body: Most names have no article. A fixed set of name types does.
cards.body_cz: Většina jmen je bez členu. Pevná skupina typů jmen člen má.

rows: the Vietnam War · the Second World War
the CIA · the BBC · the USA

cards.title: Institutions and routines: no article
cards.body: When you use a place for its purpose, the noun loses its article. The same word with `the` means the building.
cards.body_cz: Když místo používáte k jeho účelu, jméno ztrácí člen. Totéž slovo s `the` znamená budovu.

rows: I've only been inside a church once.
The college is on the hill.

points: last / next / this + time: last weekend · next week · this morning — no article

cards.title: Talking in general: no article
cards.body: A plural or uncountable noun with no article means the thing in general. Putting `the` in front points at particular ones — the most common Czech-speaker error in this set.
cards.body_cz: Množné číslo nebo nepočitatelné jméno bez členu znamená věc obecně. `the` před ním ukazuje na konkrétní — nejčastější chyba českých mluvčích v této sadě.

rows: He brings mice into the house.
The mice in the kitchen are huge.

cards.title: Two small traps: a few · jobs
cards.title_cz: Dvě malé pasti: a few · povolání
cards.body: Both are places where Czech says nothing and English needs `a`.
cards.body_cz: V obou případech čeština neříká nic a angličtina potřebuje `a`.
points: a few days = several days (neutral) · few days = hardly any days (negative)
work as a cleaner · she is a nurse · he became an engineer — jobs always take a/an
